effects.log: Huiming bows and writes your name on the donor's board, at the top, in gold.

choices.text: Ask every household to give one copper object

effects.log: Pots, hairpins, door rings and one ancestral spittoon pile up at the temple. It is everyone's bell now.

choices.text: Tell the abbot the bell sounds fine

effects.log: Huiming listens to the bell, then to you, and leaves with the same smile. The bell clanks on.

events.text: The bellfounder from the county town casts it in a pit by the temple. On the day of the pour, the bronze is short; the mould will not fill. The crowd watches the founder's face go grey. The bronze glows in the crucible like a setting sun.
events.arc: The Cracked Bell of Clear Spring

choices.text: Throw your own silver bracelet into the crucible

effects.log: The crowd gasps, then follows: rings, coins, a child's lock charm. The mould fills to the lip.

choices.text: Pour it short and call it a small bell

effects.log: The bell comes out a hand smaller, and sounds higher, like a bird. People grow to love it.

choices.text: Stop the pour and recast tomorrow

ok.log: The founder adds tin overnight. The second pour is perfect, and the bell rings true and deep.

fail.log: The second pour cracks in the cooling. The founder weeps. Third time lucky, at your expense.

events.text: Years later, on a dry autumn night, a fire starts in the granary row. The new bell of Clear Spring rings without stopping, and every household of {ct_fief} comes running with buckets, because every household knows that bell.
events.arc: The Cracked Bell of Clear Spring

choices.text: Join the bucket line

effects.log: You pass buckets until dawn between a blacksmith and a nun. The granary row is saved, all but one shed.

choices.text: Order a fire watch and a water tank by the granaries

effects.log: Next spring a stone tank stands by the granaries. The bell has never rung for fire since.

choices.text: Thank the people at the temple: their copper saved the town

effects.log: The abbot rings the bell once for every household that gave. It takes most of the morning.

events.text: One morning a notice is pasted on the mill door of {ct_fief}, in a good hand: "Tax the steward, not the plough." By noon there are four more. By evening the miller has stopped scraping them off and started reading them aloud.

choices.text: Lower the grain tax a tenth

effects.log: The notices stop for a month. Then a new one: "A tenth is a start."

choices.text: Find out who writes in such a good hand

effects.log: There are only three people in {ct_fief} who write that well. One of them is the village schoolteacher, Teacher Lin.

choices.text: Double the night patrols

effects.log: The patrols find no one. The notices go up anyway, now with a drawing of a patrol, looking lost.

events.text: Word comes of a meeting in Old Hu's barn after the full moon. Farmers, carters, a few of your own militia. They mean to march on the hall at harvest and ask for the steward's books, in person, with torches.

choices.text: Go to the barn yourself, in a farmer's cloak

effects.log: You stand at the back. Teacher Lin speaks well and angrily, and is right about half of it.

choices.text: Arrest the leaders before the march

effects.log: Six men are taken in the night. The barn is empty after that; the anger is not.

choices.text: Invite Teacher Lin to the hall to talk

effects.log: Lin comes, stiff as a brush, and talks for three hours. You learn more of your own fief than in three years.

events.text: At harvest the torches come anyway, three hundred of them, up the road to your gate. They are quiet. They carry hoes but hold them low. At the front stands Teacher Lin, holding a scroll of grievances like a banner.

choices.text: Open the gate and walk out to meet them alone

ok.log: You read the scroll by torchlight, in front of all of them, and agree to four points of seven. The torches go home.

fail.log: They hear you out, but the crowd is tired and angry. A stone breaks your lantern; the night ends in a shoving match.

choices.text: Read Lin's grievances aloud, point by point, and answer each one

effects.log: You answer every point you heard in the barn before Lin can make it. The crowd laughs, then listens, then goes home.

choices.text: Bar the gate and wait for morning

effects.log: The torches burn down outside your gate. At dawn the road is empty, and so is the goodwill.

events.text: The harvest is in, the hall still stands, and Teacher Lin is still teaching sums to the children of {ct_fief}. The steward's books, you notice, have been very honest this year. Lin bows to you in the street now, stiffly, as one bows to a difficult colleague.

choices.text: Make Lin the fief's new clerk of accounts

effects.log: Lin accepts with a scowl. The accounts have never been so honest, or so rudely written.

choices.text: Leave Lin at the school

effects.log: Lin teaches the children to read. Some of them, one day, will paste better notices than their teacher.

choices.text: Keep a quiet eye on Lin from now on

effects.log: A militiaman sits outside the school every afternoon. Lin brings him tea, pointedly.

events.text: The boundary stone between {ct_fief} and the neighbouring estate has walked two hundred paces in the night, taking the whole Mulberry Valley with it. The neighbouring Viscount, {npc}, sends a polite note claiming the valley by an old map.

choices.text: Have the stone carried back at once

effects.log: Your men carry the stone back. The next morning it has walked again. This could go on.

choices.text: Take the claim to the prefecture court

effects.log: The prefect accepts your petition and sets a hearing for spring. Meanwhile {npc}'s goats graze the valley.

choices.text: Ride over and invite {npc} to settle it at archery

effects.log: {npc} laughs and accepts. Three arrows each, at the stone itself.

events.text: The matter comes to a head at the valley itself, with the stone sitting between you and {npc}. {npc} unrolls the old map. There is a large tea stain exactly where the border ought to be. Both your stewards lean in to look, and both groan.

choices.text: Shoot your three arrows at the stone

ok.log: Three arrows, three hits. {npc} sighs, shoots two hits and a miss, and the valley is yours.

fail.log: Two of yours miss. {npc} shoots three true, and bows. The valley goes to the neighbour.

choices.text: Bring the oldest shepherd in the valley as a witness

effects.log: Old Shepherd Gu, ninety-one, points to a crooked pine. "Stone stood there. My grandfather tethered the family goats to it." The court accepts this.

choices.text: Bribe the court clerk to find a better map (80 taels)

effects.log: A much better map is found, without tea. {npc} looks at it and smiles thinly.

events.text: A year later {npc} rides over alone, without the old map. The Mulberry Valley, {npc} says, has silkworms on one side and mulberries on the other, and neither of you can work it without the other. The goats, meanwhile, have eaten half of each.

choices.text: Propose sharing the valley and the silk

effects.log: You and {npc} plant the valley together. The stone stays where it is, and nobody moves it again.

choices.text: Refuse: the valley is yours

effects.log: {npc} rides home. For twenty years the two estates trade nothing but cold letters.

choices.text: Confess the bought map, and offer half the valley

effects.log: {npc} is silent, then laughs. "I moved the stone," {npc} says. "We are even." The valley is shared.

events.text: The snow comes in the ninth month, a full moon early, and does not stop. The granary of {ct_fief} holds enough for half the winter. The roads south, where rice is cheap, will close within the week. The old people say they have seen such a winter once before, and do not say how it ended.

choices.text: Send carts south for rice before the roads close (200 taels)

effects.log: The last carts come in through snow up to the axles. It is not enough, but it is something.

choices.text: Open your deer park to the villagers for hunting

effects.log: The deer of your grandfather's park feed {ct_fief} through the eleventh month. The park is empty by the twelfth.

choices.text: Ration strictly from the granary

effects.log: One bowl a day, measured by your own clerks. People are hungry, and alive, and counting.

events.text: By midwinter the villages are boiling elm bark. A grain merchant arrives on a sledge offering rice at three times the autumn price. The same week, a mountain sect sends word: it will take forty children as disciples, and feed them.

choices.text: Pay the merchant's price (150 taels)

effects.log: The merchant leaves rich. Every village eats rice for a month, and curses the merchant, and blesses you.

choices.text: Let the families choose whether to send children to the sect

effects.log: Thirty-one children go up the mountain in the snow. Their parents walk with them to the first bend and no further.

choices.text: Seize the merchant's rice and pay the autumn price

effects.log: The merchant screams about the law. The rice feeds the villages. The province will hear of it.

events.text: Spring. The snow melts off the hills and the headmen bring you the count. Fewer were lost in {ct_fief} than in the counties around it, but there are new graves on every hill, and an old man asks where the names should go.

choices.text: Raise a memorial stone with every name

effects.log: The stone stands by the granary, so that whoever holds the keys must read it every morning.

choices.text: Build a second granary, so it never happens again (120 taels)

effects.log: The new granary is filled before the next frost. Nobody in {ct_fief} ever boils bark again.

choices.text: Ride up the mountain to visit the children at the sect

effects.log: The thirty-one are thin no longer, and hold their wooden swords proudly. You carry their parents' letters both ways.

events.text: On petition day in {ct_fief} the line goes out of the hall and around the well. First come the brothers Zhou, who have stopped speaking to each other but share one pear orchard their late father left them, and one ladder.

choices.text: Divide the orchard down the middle with a rope

effects.log: The rope goes up. The elder brother gets the big trees; the younger gets the well. Both are furious.

choices.text: Order them to work it together for one year

effects.log: The brothers glare at you, then at each other, then pick up the ladder from opposite ends.

choices.text: Ask what the father would have wanted

effects.log: The brothers argue about that for an hour, in front of the whole line. You hear the next petition while they shout.

events.text: The Zhou brothers return. The pears this year are the finest in the county, and the brothers still cannot agree on a single thing, including the price, the market, and whose turn it is with the ladder.

choices.text: Buy them a second ladder (5 taels)

effects.log: A second ladder ends half the argument. The other half is about whose ladder is better.

choices.text: Make the elder brother sell and the younger brother pick

effects.log: Each now depends on the other completely. They hate it, and earn twice as much.

choices.text: Take the rope down and see what happens

effects.log: Without the rope, the two halves grow back into one orchard. The brothers keep walking around where it was.

choices.text: Tell them to settle it or the orchard reverts to you

effects.log: The brothers settle it in one evening. Fear is a fine mediator.

events.text: Years later, the younger Zhou brother falls sick. The elder carries him to the physician on his back, nine li, then sits in the pear orchard alone and picks the whole crop himself. At petition day he comes to you with a basket of pears.

choices.text: Accept the pears, and ask about the brother

effects.log: "Recovering," says the elder Zhou. "Complaining already." It is the first time you have seen him smile.

choices.text: Send your own physician to the younger brother

effects.log: Your physician visits every week. The younger Zhou recovers and sends twice as many pears, with a note: "His were bruised."

choices.text: Have the pears served at your next banquet

effects.log: Your guests ask where the pears are from. You tell the whole story, and it becomes a famous one.

events.text: A silk merchant from the south, Master Qiao, walks the fields of {ct_fief} with a handful of soil and a calculating smile. "Millet," Qiao says, as if it were a disease. Plant mulberry, raise silkworms, and in five years the fief will be twice as rich.

choices.text: Plant half the fields with mulberry

effects.log: Half the millet goes under. The farmers plant saplings and look at the sky, unconvinced.

choices.text: Plant all of it

effects.log: Every field of {ct_fief} becomes a young orchard. There is no millet this year at all. People buy their rice and pray.

choices.text: Thank Qiao, and keep the millet

effects.log: Qiao leaves with the same smile. Millet, at least, has never gone out of fashion.

events.text: The mulberries are grown and the first silkworms are hatching in every loft of {ct_fief}, when a blight comes up from the south: the leaves curl and blacken. The worms will starve in a week. Qiao's letters have stopped coming.

choices.text: Have every leaf washed in lime water, as the old texts say

ok.log: It works, mostly. Two lofts in three are saved, and the first silk is spun by autumn.

fail.log: The lime burns half the leaves the blight did not. Most of the worms are lost.

choices.text: Buy leaves from the next county at any price (100 taels)

effects.log: Carts of leaves arrive daily from strangers. The worms eat, and spin, and the silk is saved.

choices.text: Ask Qiao, who must have seen this before

effects.log: Qiao has, and sends a remedy of smoke and ash. It works, and Qiao asks for a tenth of the silk in thanks.

events.text: The silk of {ct_fief} sells well in the capital now. The women who reel it in the silk house come to your hall together, twenty of them, with sore hands. They want wages, not shares of the family's harvest.

choices.text: Grant them wages of their own

effects.log: Twenty women are paid in their own names. Some of them buy land. The fathers of {ct_fief} are scandalised.

choices.text: Refuse: the old ways keep families together

effects.log: The women go back to the reels in silence. Next year, three of them leave for the city's silk houses.

choices.text: Grant wages, and plant the millet back on the hills too

effects.log: Silk in the valleys, millet on the hills. If the silk ever fails, nobody will starve.

events.text: A grizzled veteran named Hou turns up at the gate of {ct_fief}, with one eye, a frontier medal, and an offer: for a roof and a jar of rice wine a month, Hou will turn your farmers into a militia that could stop a bandit army.

choices.text: Hire Hou

effects.log: Hou moves into the gatehouse that afternoon and asks to see the farmers. All of them. At dawn.

choices.text: Ask to see what Hou can do first

effects.log: Hou knocks down your three best guards with a broom, then apologises to the broom.

choices.text: Refuse: farmers should farm

effects.log: Hou shrugs and walks on to the next county, which hires Hou within the week.

events.text: Hou's first drill goes badly. Forty farmers with hoes, rakes and one butter churn cannot tell left from right, and the oxen have wandered into the line. Hou has tied a straw to every farmer's left arm.

choices.text: Join the drill yourself, with a straw on your arm

effects.log: The farmers see you march and stop laughing. By evening they turn left together, mostly.

choices.text: Pay for real spears instead of hoes (60 taels)

effects.log: Real spears arrive. The farmers hold them like hoes, but at least they are pointy.

choices.text: Let Hou drill them through the slack season

effects.log: Three months later the forty walk in step to market, and the bandits of the hills hear about it.

events.text: At harvest a band of twenty raiders comes down for the grain carts, expecting farmers. They find forty farmers, in a line, turning left together. Hou is standing in front with the butter churn handle.

choices.text: Order the militia to hold the line

effects.log: The raiders see the line, see Hou, and decide the next county has better grain.

choices.text: Lead a charge to catch the raiders

ok.log: You catch six raiders and the rest scatter. Hou says it was reckless, and gives you his own spare bowstring.

fail.log: The raiders scatter into the woods and you twist an ankle in a ditch. Hou says nothing, loudly.

choices.text: Pour Hou a whole jar of wine afterwards

effects.log: Hou drinks it all and tells stories of the frontier till dawn. Half of them might even be true.

events.text: Hou grows old in the gatehouse of {ct_fief}. The left eye is going too now, and Hou drills the militia by voice alone, from a stool, and still catches every farmer who turns right. The militia ask whether the drill ground might bear Hou's name.

choices.text: Name it Hou's Field, with a stone

effects.log: The stone says Hou's Field. Hou pretends to be annoyed and sits beside it every evening.

choices.text: Ask Hou to choose a successor from the militia

effects.log: Hou picks the butter-churn farmer, of all people. The farmer drills them harder than Hou ever did.

choices.text: Pour Hou a jar of the best wine in the hall (20 taels)

effects.log: Hou drinks it slowly and says it is the first wine worth the name in forty years.

events.text: An imperial assessor arrives in {ct_fief} with two clerks and a measuring rope dyed red, to re-measure every field for the land tax. Assessor Peng has a cold, a short temper, and a reputation for measuring very generously in the throne's favour.
events.arc: The Assessor With a Measuring Rope

choices.text: Give Peng the best rooms and the best food

effects.log: Peng eats well and sniffles less. The rope, oddly, seems to shrink by a tenth.

choices.text: Ride with Peng and check every measurement

effects.log: You ride the fields with Peng for a month, rope in hand. Peng hates you, and measures fairly.

choices.text: Offer Peng a quiet gift (100 taels)

effects.log: The gift is accepted without a word. The rope shrinks by a quarter.

events.text: Peng's report goes to the capital. A month later a letter comes back: the throne is pleased, the land tax of {ct_fief} is set, and a second assessor will visit next year, to "confirm" the first. Your clerks read the word "confirm" several times, uneasily.
events.arc: The Assessor With a Measuring Rope

choices.text: Prepare honestly for the second visit

effects.log: Your clerks re-measure every field themselves. The numbers are your own, and you can live with them.

choices.text: Write to Peng for advice

effects.log: Peng writes back three lines: "Measure honestly. The second is my cousin. He is worse."

choices.text: Panic about the bribe

effects.log: The second assessor is coming to measure the first assessor's rope. You sleep badly for a year.

events.text: The second assessor is Peng's cousin, younger, sharper, and colder. Field by field the new rope stretches. At the last field the cousin rolls it up and looks at you, waiting. The rope, you notice, is a different colour from Peng's, and a good deal longer.
events.arc: The Assessor With a Measuring Rope

choices.text: Show the cousin your own clerks' honest measures

ok.log: The cousin compares the books for a night and signs yours. "Rare," the cousin says. It is meant as praise.

fail.log: The cousin prefers the rope. The tax goes up a fifth.

choices.text: Pay what the rope says

effects.log: The tax of {ct_fief} goes up a fifth. The farmers grumble, but at least it is honest grumbling.

choices.text: Confess the bribe before the cousin finds it

effects.log: The cousin stares, then writes it down without expression. Peng is recalled. Your tax goes up a third.

events.text: A shepherd's goats of {ct_fief} will not leave one muddy hollow on Crow Hill. The shepherd tastes the mud, then runs to the hall: a salt spring. Salt is an imperial monopoly; a private salt well is a crime that ends families.
events.arc: The Salt Spring of Crow Hill

choices.text: Report the spring to the Salt Commission

effects.log: The Commission sends an officer and a cartload of seals. It will be the throne's well, with your people working it.

choices.text: Cover the hollow and tell the shepherd to forget it

effects.log: The shepherd forgets, mostly. The goats do not.

choices.text: Boil a little salt in secret for {ct_fief}'s own kitchens

effects.log: A pot of grey salt boils in the back of the hall. It tastes of iron and danger.

events.text: Two years pass. A Salt Commission inspector rides through {ct_fief} on the way to somewhere else, and stops to water a horse at the foot of Crow Hill. The horse will not stop licking the stones. The goats watch it with professional interest.
events.arc: The Salt Spring of Crow Hill

choices.text: Show the inspector the Commission's own well and seals

effects.log: The inspector smiles at the official seals and rides on. Honesty, for once, is also convenient.

choices.text: Invite the inspector to dinner, far from the hill

ok.log: The inspector eats, drinks, and leaves in the morning with a full stomach and no questions.

fail.log: At dinner the inspector asks about the salt in the soup. It is grey.

choices.text: Report the spring now, as if newly found

effects.log: The inspector takes the report with one raised eyebrow. The well is the throne's now, and so is the suspicion.

events.text: The matter of the salt spring reaches its end. The Commission's well on Crow Hill now employs thirty families of {ct_fief}, or the spring is a quiet hollow, or a letter has come from the prefecture with a red seal.
events.arc: The Salt Spring of Crow Hill

choices.text: Open the letter with the red seal

effects.log: A fine of three hundred taels, and a warning. It could have been much worse.

choices.text: Visit the thirty families at the well

effects.log: The salt workers have new roofs and white hands. They call the hill Goat Hill now, in honour of the goats.

choices.text: Walk up to the hollow on your own

effects.log: The goats are still there, licking the mud. You sit with them a while. A fief has many secrets; this is a small one.

events.text: On the road, far from the fief you lost, a farmer catches up with you, out of breath. It is old Liu from the bean fields, who has walked four days with a sack of roasted chestnuts. "They are not ours any more," Liu says, "but the tree did not know."

choices.text: Eat the chestnuts with Liu by the road

effects.log: You eat them warm by the roadside. Liu tells you every name in the village, and who has married whom.

choices.text: Send Liu home with silver for the village (40 taels)

effects.log: Liu refuses three times, then takes it, and walks back four days. The silver buys seed for the spring.

choices.text: Tell Liu not to come again: it is over

effects.log: Liu nods slowly and goes. You keep one chestnut in your sleeve for a year.

events.text: News from the old fief reaches you in pieces: the new master doubled the grain tax, sold the deer park, and pulled down the bell tower for its bronze. The people ask, in a letter with forty thumbprints, whether you will come back.

choices.text: Write back: wait, and keep your heads down

effects.log: Your letter goes back with Liu's cousin. They will wait. They are good at it.

choices.text: Petition the court to have the fief restored

effects.log: Your petition joins a pile of others in the capital. A clerk tells you it may be read in ten years.

choices.text: Ride back in secret to see it for yourself

effects.log: The village is thinner, quieter. Children who did not know you stare. The bell tower is a stump.

events.text: A year on, word comes that the new master of your old fief has fallen out of favour and fled. The people have shut the gates against the tax collectors and sent for you. The road back is open, if you have the nerve to take it.

choices.text: Go back and speak for the people before the prefect

ok.log: The prefect hears you, sees the forty thumbprints, and writes to the capital in your favour. It is a beginning.

fail.log: The prefect hears you out and sends you away with tea. The fief goes to a cousin of the chancellor.

choices.text: Go back as a neighbour, not a master, and help rebuild the bell tower

effects.log: You carry stones with the villagers. Nobody calls you anything, which is the best title you have had.

choices.text: Stay away: it is theirs now

effects.log: You send Liu a letter and a bag of chestnut seedlings. The new trees, they say, are doing well.

events.text: In a pawnshop in a market town, behind the jade bracelets, you see it: the bronze seal of the fief you lost, its lion handle worn smooth by your thumb. The pawnbroker, a fat cheerful man, wants two hundred taels.

choices.text: Buy it back (200 taels)

effects.log: The seal is heavy in your sleeve on the road home. It opens nothing now. It is still yours.

choices.text: Ask the pawnbroker who brought it in

effects.log: A steward, the pawnbroker says, very nervous, in the spring. A steward of the new master.

choices.text: Walk away

effects.log: You walk out without looking back. You dream about the lion handle for a week.

events.text: The pawned seal is the end of a thread. The new master's steward has been selling everything with a stamp on it, including, it seems, the deeds of the village fields. Somewhere, the people of your old fief are losing their land on paper.

choices.text: Track the steward down

effects.log: You find the steward in a gambling house, owing more than the fief is worth. The deeds are in a bag by the dice.

choices.text: Warn the village headmen by letter

effects.log: The headmen hide the true field maps under the temple floor. Paper fights paper.

choices.text: Write to the prefect about the stolen seal

effects.log: The prefect writes back politely that the seal belongs to the new master. Nothing comes of it.

events.text: Whatever came of the seal, you end the matter on a cold morning in your rented rooms, the lion handle in your palm or only in your memory, with a choice about what a lost title is still good for. Outside, the market town goes about its business.

choices.text: Win the deeds from the steward at dice

ok.log: You win the bag in three throws. The deeds go back to the villages that night, by fast rider.

fail.log: You lose the throw, and the steward takes the deeds to a moneylender in the city.

choices.text: Buy the deeds outright and burn them (150 taels)

effects.log: The deeds burn in a brazier. Without them, the fields belong to the people who plough them.

choices.text: Press the old seal on a letter to the village

effects.log: The lion prints one last time on cheap paper: "I have not forgotten you." They frame it.

choices.text: Let it go: titles are paper, too

effects.log: You go out and buy hot congee instead. It is the best meal you have had in a year.

events.text: At the Prefect's spring banquet, the seating chart puts you one place below the Count of Eastern Ridge, whose title is two years newer than yours. Every noble in the hall has noticed. The Count has noticed most of all, and is smiling.

choices.text: Sit, eat, and say nothing

effects.log: You eat in perfect silence. Everyone admires your dignity, and the Count is mildly disappointed.

choices.text: Point out the error to the Prefect's steward

effects.log: The steward goes pale, checks the patent of nobility, and moves you. The Count's smile freezes.

choices.text: Swap seats with the Count's wife and talk to her about horses

effects.log: You spend the banquet discussing horses. The Count spends it next to an empty seat.

events.text: The seating war spreads. At the Mid-Autumn banquet the Count arrives early and sits on your cushion. At the New Year banquet you arrive earlier. The Prefect, in despair, proposes a round table. The cushion makers of the prefecture have never been busier.

choices.text: Support the round table

effects.log: A round table is carried in. Everyone is equally important, and therefore everyone sulks.

choices.text: Arrive at dawn and sit in the best seat

effects.log: You sit in an empty hall for six hours. When the Count arrives, it is worth it.

choices.text: Send the Count a gift of a very small cushion

effects.log: The Count receives a cushion the size of a teacup. The whole prefecture laughs for a month.

events.text: The Count of Eastern Ridge falls ill that winter, and asks, of all people, for you. Propped in bed, the Count says the seating feud was the most fun of the last ten years, and asks who will sit in that place at the banquets now.

choices.text: Promise to keep the Count's seat warm

effects.log: The Count laughs until it turns into coughing. At the next banquet you leave the seat empty, with a cup.

choices.text: Bring the very small cushion back

effects.log: The Count holds the tiny cushion and laughs and laughs. It is buried with the Count, a year later.

choices.text: Talk of other things

effects.log: You talk of horses and harvests until the lamp burns low. Nothing about seats at all.

events.text: A house with a title needs a banner, and your household has none. The court embroiderer, Embroiderer Shen, unrolls designs on your floor: a crane, a tiger, a carp leaping a waterfall, and, for some reason, a cabbage.

choices.text: The crane: long life and dignity

effects.log: The crane is chosen. Embroiderer Shen nods approvingly; cranes are very popular this year.

choices.text: The tiger: let rivals think twice

effects.log: The tiger is chosen. Your servants begin, unconsciously, to walk more fiercely.

choices.text: The cabbage

effects.log: Embroiderer Shen explains that the cabbage means a hundred kinds of wealth. You choose it, and become a little famous.

events.text: The banner is finished: one bolt of silk, three months of needlework. The household motto must go along the border. The steward proposes "Loyal to the Throne". Your oldest servant suggests something truer.

choices.text: "Loyal to the Throne"

effects.log: Safe, correct, and exactly the same as eleven other houses. The censors approve.

choices.text: "We Remember"

effects.log: Two words, short and strange. Guests ask what you remember, and you never quite say.

choices.text: "A Hundred Kinds of Wealth"

effects.log: The cabbage and its motto become a joke, then a legend. Merchants want to dine with the cabbage house.

events.text: At the Duke's hunting festival, a rival house parades a banner with a tiger eating a crane. The insult is clear to every noble on the field, and every noble on the field turns, very politely, to see what you will do.

choices.text: Have your crane banner raised higher

effects.log: Your servants hold the crane higher than the tiger, all afternoon, arms shaking. It is a moral victory.

choices.text: Ride over and compliment the embroidery

effects.log: You praise the stitching so lavishly that the insult dissolves into embarrassment. The rival house goes red.

choices.text: Raise your own tiger beside theirs

effects.log: Two tigers glare across the hunting field. The Duke laughs and declares it a draw.

choices.text: Ignore it and hunt

effects.log: You take the best stag of the day. Nobody remembers the banner, only the stag.

events.text: House Mo has been the rival of your house for three generations, over a mill, a marriage and a misread poem. Its new heir, {npc}, sends you a jar of tea and a letter proposing to end the feud. The tea is excellent. The letter is very short.

choices.text: Accept the tea and invite {npc} to dinner

effects.log: {npc} comes to dinner, alone, and eats everything, including the garnish. It is a start.

choices.text: Send back a jar of your own, better tea

effects.log: {npc} replies with better tea still. Within a year, both houses own the best tea in the province.

choices.text: Ignore it: three generations do not end in one letter

effects.log: The feud continues. Your grandchildren will inherit it, along with the mill.

events.text: At the provincial hunt, a boar breaks from cover and charges straight at {npc}, who has dismounted to fix a stirrup. You are the only rider close enough. The boar is the size of a millstone and in a very bad temper. The servants of both houses freeze.

choices.text: Ride the boar down

ok.log: You turn the boar with your spear a pace from {npc}. The whole hunt cheers, both houses together.

fail.log: You turn the boar, but your horse falls. {npc} drags you clear of the hooves.

choices.text: Shout a warning

effects.log: {npc} vaults into a tree just in time, and spends the rest of the hunt being teased for it.

choices.text: Do nothing: let the boar decide the feud

effects.log: The boar misses. {npc} looks at you across the clearing and understands exactly what you did not do.

events.text: The old heads of both houses are gone now, and {npc} sits across a table from you with the deed to the mill that started it all, sixty years ago. {npc} pushes it halfway across the table and waits. Outside, the mill wheel turns.

choices.text: Push it back: the mill should belong to {npc}'s house

effects.log: {npc} laughs for the first time you have heard. The two houses hold a joint banquet, and the old poem is read correctly at last.

choices.text: Propose running the mill together

effects.log: The mill runs for both houses. The miller is paid twice, by mistake, for a year, and says nothing.

choices.text: Take the deed, and owe {npc} a life

effects.log: "You saved mine," {npc} says. "Now we are even, and friends." The deed is yours; so is the friendship.

events.text: The campaign against {ct_foe} lives or dies on rice, and the rice is two hundred carts stuck in a valley of mud behind you. {ct_unit} is ordered to bring it forward. The oxen are tired, the carters are frightened, and the scouts have seen riders on the ridge.

choices.text: Put {ct_unit} in the mud beside the oxen and push

effects.log: Soldiers push, oxen pull, carters swear. The train moves a li a day, and nobody complains of being idle.

choices.text: Send half the unit up the ridge to watch the riders

effects.log: Your men crouch on the ridge in the rain. The riders see them, and decide against it for now.

choices.text: Burn the slowest carts to move faster

effects.log: Forty carts burn by the road. The rest move faster. The quartermaster will never forgive you.

events.text: At the river ford a rider gallops up: the main army is starving and wants the rice in three days. The road is five days. There is a shorter way, over the Ghost Pass, where the carts may not fit and the enemy may be waiting.

choices.text: Take the Ghost Pass

ok.log: The carts scrape through with a finger's width to spare. You reach the army in three days, to a roar.

fail.log: Ten carts tumble into the gorge. The rest arrive a day late, and the general says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Keep to the road and send the fastest carts ahead

effects.log: Twenty light carts race ahead and arrive on the third day. The rest follow. It is enough.

choices.text: Keep to the road at the train's pace

effects.log: You arrive in five days. The army has eaten its horses' oats and is not grateful.

events.text: Two nights from the army, the riders from the ridge finally come, thirty of them, with torches for the rice. The carters dive under the carts. {ct_unit} has to hold the line of carts for an hour. The oxen, sensibly, lie down.

choices.text: Form the carts into a ring and fight from inside it

effects.log: The ring holds. The riders circle it twice, lose four men, and vanish into the dark.

choices.text: Signal the men on the ridge to fall on their rear

effects.log: Your men come down off the ridge behind the riders. It is over in minutes, and the rice is safe.

choices.text: Sacrifice twenty carts to save the rest

effects.log: The riders burn twenty carts and ride off, satisfied. The rest roll on, smelling of smoke.

events.text: The rice reaches the army. That night every soldier eats a full bowl for the first time in a month, and the general himself walks down the line of cooking fires to find the officer who brought it. The cooks are crying into the steam.

choices.text: Give the credit to the carters and the oxen

effects.log: The general laughs and orders the oxen an extra measure of beans. The carters drink to you all night.

choices.text: Report the journey in full, every cart and every day

effects.log: The general reads your report and keeps it, as an example of how it should be done.

choices.text: Eat your own bowl in peace

effects.log: You eat slowly, by a fire, among your men. The general passes you by without knowing. You do not mind.

events.text: On the march against {ct_foe}, your patrol drags a young soldier out of a millet field, three days absent, holding a bag of dry bread. The name is {npc}, from a village two days back. The law of the army for desertion on campaign is death.

choices.text: Report {npc} to the provost

effects.log: The provost writes the name down. {npc} is taken to the stockade, looking straight ahead.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why

effects.log: "My village is on the enemy's road," {npc} says. "Nobody else was going to warn them."

choices.text: Write {npc} down as returned from a scouting errand

effects.log: The ledger now says {npc} was scouting. {npc} stares at you, then at the ledger, and says nothing.

events.text: {npc}'s village is on the enemy's road, as {npc} said. Your scouts confirm it: riders of the enemy are two days from it, and the village has not moved. {npc}'s fate, and theirs, are still in your hands.

choices.text: Speak for {npc} at the provost's tribunal

effects.log: You speak of the village and the warning. The tribunal reduces it to forty strokes and a fine.

choices.text: Send {npc} with a patrol to warn the village, officially this time

effects.log: {npc} rides out in front, white-faced, and comes back two days later. The village is in the hills.

choices.text: Keep {npc} close and say nothing more

effects.log: {npc} marches beside you every day after, and works harder than any soldier in the line.

events.text: In the last battle of the campaign, a spear comes at you from the side, out of the dust, and someone throws themselves in the way. It is {npc}, who takes the blow on a shield and keeps both of you on your feet.

choices.text: Put {npc} forward for a merit citation

effects.log: The citation reads: for courage. Nobody mentions the millet field, ever again.

choices.text: Make {npc} your own runner

effects.log: {npc} becomes the fastest runner in the army. Every message you send arrives early.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the ledger is now true

effects.log: "You were scouting," you say. {npc} grins, the first grin of the campaign. "I was, wasn't I."

events.text: Your scouts come in at dusk with the enemy's order of battle. The senior scout swears {ct_foe} are forming {ct_scouted}. A junior scout, a quiet woman from the hill country named Yan, says nothing until asked, then says the senior is wrong.

choices.text: Trust the senior scout

effects.log: The senior scout's report goes up to the general's tent with your seal on it.

choices.text: Send Yan back out to look again, tonight

effects.log: Yan goes out alone into the dark with a coil of rope and a dry biscuit.

choices.text: Ride out to see for yourself

effects.log: You lie in wet grass on a hill until dawn, watching the enemy fires. The pattern is not clear.

events.text: At dawn the picture sharpens. The enemy's front is drawn up as the senior scout said, but behind a fold of the hills there is a second line of fires, set apart, the kind a reserve would make before turning into a different shape.

choices.text: Order your line to counter the front as reported

effects.log: Your line is set to beat the shape the scouts saw. It is the safe report and the safe order.

choices.text: Hold a reserve to match the hidden line

effects.log: You keep a third of your strength back, hidden, in case the enemy changes shape.

choices.text: Hear Yan's report: the hidden line is the real shape

effects.log: Yan comes back muddy to the knees. "They will turn at noon," Yan says. "They always turn at noon."

events.text: At noon the enemy line wheels into a new shape, exactly as Yan said. A Wedge would break a Fish Scale; a Fish Scale would wrap a Crane Wing; a Crane Wing would swallow a Long Snake; a Long Snake would coil around a Wedge. You have minutes.

choices.text: Read the new shape and answer it

ok.log: You call the right shape in time. The enemy's turn becomes their undoing, and the field is yours.

fail.log: You call it a heartbeat late. The line holds, barely, and both sides withdraw at dusk.

choices.text: Spring the reserve you were ready to use

effects.log: Your hidden reserve hits the turning line in its flank. It is over before it begins.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them come

effects.log: You hold. It is ugly and slow, and at dusk the enemy pulls back. Nobody wins.

events.text: The army must cross the Yellow Ferry, a river half a li wide and the colour of millet porridge, with {ct_foe} watching from the far bank. The engineers can build a bridge of boats in four days. The general wants it in two.

choices.text: Work the engineers in shifts, day and night

effects.log: By lamplight and dawn the bridge grows, boat by boat. The men sleep standing up.

choices.text: Light false campfires downstream to draw the enemy

effects.log: A hundred fires burn on an empty bank downstream. The enemy watches them all night.

choices.text: Find the old ferrymen who know the shallows

effects.log: An old ferryman named Kong, missing four teeth, knows a ford the maps forgot.

events.text: On the second night, the bridge is three boats short of the far bank. The river is rising from rain in the mountains. Old Kong says the ford will close by dawn. Across the water, the enemy's horns begin.

choices.text: Lead the first company through Kong's ford

ok.log: You wade through chest-deep water with {ct_unit} and take the far bank before the enemy wakes.

fail.log: The current takes your footing and three men with it. The rest reach the bank, half drowned.

choices.text: Rope the last boats across by swimmers

effects.log: Twenty swimmers drag the last boats into place under a rain of arrows. The bridge is whole by dawn.

choices.text: Wait for daylight

effects.log: You wait. By morning the bridge is finished, and the enemy is waiting on the far side.

events.text: Dawn on the river. The bridge of boats sways under marching feet. Your half of the army is across; the other half is on the bridge when the enemy's riders come down to the water, straight at the bridgehead.

choices.text: Hold the bridgehead with spears

effects.log: Your spears hold the bridgehead for an hour, until the whole army is across. The riders break.

choices.text: Strike the riders from the downstream flank

effects.log: The enemy riders, who spent the night watching your false fires, are tired and slow. You hit them in the flank.

choices.text: Cut the bridge behind you to force the men forward

effects.log: The bridge drifts away. With no way back, the army goes forward like a flood. It is very effective, and very cruel.

events.text: The river is crossed, the enemy driven back. On the bank lie the men who did not make it, wrapped in their own cloaks. Old Kong, the ferryman, asks if he might take them home across the water, one boat at a time.

choices.text: Let Kong take them, and pay him well (40 taels)

effects.log: Kong ferries them back over three days, singing a ferryman's song to each one. The army hears it from camp.

choices.text: Bury them on the bank with a stone

effects.log: A stone stands at the Yellow Ferry with the names. Ferrymen still bow to it when they pass.

choices.text: Write to each family yourself

effects.log: You write sixty letters by lamplight. Each one says something true about the soldier. It takes all night.

events.text: The new recruits of {ct_unit} cannot remember the formation circle. In the campaign against {ct_foe}, that will kill them. Sergeant Kui, a patient woman with a voice like a gong, is teaching it with four pebbles on a drumhead.

choices.text: Sit and watch Kui teach

effects.log: "The Wedge splits the Fish Scale," Kui says, pushing a pebble. "The Fish Scale wraps the Crane Wing." The recruits nod at the pebbles.

choices.text: Make up a rhyme for the circle

effects.log: "Wedge cuts the Fish, the Fish nets the Crane, the Crane eats the Snake, the Snake chokes the Wedge again." The camp sings it all week.

choices.text: Drill it in the field instead, with real ranks

effects.log: The recruits run into each other for a day. By evening, they understand the circle in their legs.

events.text: The recruits play the circle as a game around the fires: one calls a shape, the other must answer it in a breath. A loud recruit named Fu wins every night and is getting unbearable about it. Fu has started calling the shapes in a sing-song voice.

choices.text: Challenge Fu yourself

effects.log: You answer every call in half a breath. Fu goes quiet, then asks you to teach the trick.

choices.text: Let Fu teach the slow ones

effects.log: Fu turns out to be patient with the slow ones and impatient with everyone else. It is a talent.

choices.text: Call shapes that do not exist

effects.log: "Flying Turnip!" you call. Fu freezes. The whole camp laughs until they cry.

events.text: Battle. The enemy comes on in the shape the scouts foretold. Through the dust you hear the recruits of {ct_unit} muttering the circle to themselves, waiting for the drums to tell them what to become. Kui stands beside the drummer, arms folded.

choices.text: Call the counter-shape on the drums

effects.log: The drums roll the counter-shape, and the recruits fall into it without a stumble. Kui is very nearly proud.

choices.text: Have the whole line sing the rhyme as they form

effects.log: Six hundred voices sing the circle and move with it. The enemy has never seen anything like it.

choices.text: Hold the shape until the last moment, then change it

ok.log: You change at the last breath. The enemy is caught in the wrong shape and breaks.

fail.log: The change comes too late and the line buckles. It holds, but only just.

events.text: In the council tent, Marshal Gao, seventy and deaf in one ear, bangs the map table and demands a frontal charge on {ct_foe} at dawn, as in his youth. Three younger generals look at you. The map shows the enemy dug in on a ridge.
events.arc: The Old Marshal Wants a Charge

choices.text: Support the charge: Gao has the emperor's ear

effects.log: The charge is ordered. Gao beams at you all evening. The younger generals do not.

choices.text: Propose a night march around the ridge

effects.log: Gao snorts, but the younger generals rally to you. The plan is changed, barely.

choices.text: Ask Gao to tell the council about his own famous victory

effects.log: Gao tells it for an hour. In his famous victory, he went around the ridge. You let him notice that.

events.text: The battle is fought. If it was Gao's charge, the dawn was terrible: the ranks went up the ridge and many came down on stretchers. If it was your march, the enemy woke to drums behind them. Either way, Gao rode at the front, white beard flying.
events.arc: The Old Marshal Wants a Charge

choices.text: Help carry the wounded off the ridge

effects.log: You carry stretchers until noon. Gao watches from the hill, very quiet for once.

choices.text: Press the attack from behind the ridge

effects.log: The enemy, caught between two lines, breaks by noon. It is the cleanest victory of the campaign.

choices.text: Write the battle report honestly

effects.log: Your report says what happened, with numbers. It is not a popular document.

events.text: Gao summons you to the marshal's tent after the battle. The old soldier is sitting alone without armour, looking smaller. "My day is over," Gao says. "Tell me the truth: was it a good one?" A cold pot of tea sits between you.
events.arc: The Old Marshal Wants a Charge

choices.text: Tell Gao the truth

effects.log: You tell it plainly. Gao nods for a long time, then pours you tea with a steady hand.

choices.text: Tell Gao it was a fine day

effects.log: Gao smiles, and believes you, or decides to. The old marshal retires that winter, content.

choices.text: Ask Gao to teach you what the old days knew

effects.log: Gao talks till dawn: horses, rivers, the faces of old enemies. Half of it is gold.

events.text: A patrol brings in a scout of {ct_foe}, found asleep in a haystack. The prisoner's name, as near as anyone can say it, is {npc}. {npc} knows three words of Chinese: "rice", "no", and, oddly, "plum blossom".
events.arc: The Scout Who Knew Three Words

choices.text: Feed {npc} and try to talk

effects.log: {npc} eats three bowls of rice and teaches you the steppe word for "more". It is a start.

choices.text: Hand {npc} to the interrogators

effects.log: The interrogators get nothing but "no" and "plum blossom". They complain about it at dinner.

choices.text: Exchange {npc} for one of our captured men

effects.log: An exchange is arranged at a ford. {npc} walks across and waves. One of ours walks back.

events.text: Over weeks, with rice and drawings in the dirt, you and {npc} learn each other's words. {npc} draws the enemy camp: the horse lines, the chief's tent, and a wide circle of water where there is no river on your maps.
events.arc: The Scout Who Knew Three Words

choices.text: Report the hidden lake to the general

effects.log: The general studies the drawing a long time. "A lake," the general says, "would explain the horses."

choices.text: Ask {npc} why the help

effects.log: {npc} draws a little house with a plum tree. "Home," {npc} says, in Chinese, the fourth word.

choices.text: Suspect a trick and say nothing

effects.log: You keep the drawing in your sleeve and trust no one. {npc} notices, and draws nothing more.

events.text: Your army takes the hidden lake, and the enemy lose half their horses to thirst in a week. The campaign turns. {npc} watches from the prisoners' tent, with an expression you cannot read. The prisoners' tent is very quiet that week.
events.arc: The Scout Who Knew Three Words

choices.text: Tell {npc} the drawing saved many lives on both sides

effects.log: {npc} listens and says, slowly, in Chinese: "Shorter war." It is said like a prayer.

choices.text: Ask the general for {npc}'s release

effects.log: The general refuses, then relents: when the war ends. {npc} accepts this with a nod.

choices.text: Teach {npc} more words

effects.log: By spring {npc} can say twenty words, most of them about food and complaints. It is very soldierly.

events.text: The campaign is over. At the frontier gate the prisoners are released, and {npc} walks out to a horse held by an old woman of the steppe. Before mounting, {npc} turns back and holds out something small.
events.arc: The Scout Who Knew Three Words

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: It is a carved wooden plum blossom. You carry it for the rest of your life, and never explain it.

choices.text: Give {npc} a sack of rice for the road

effects.log: {npc} laughs and holds it up: "Rice!" The first word, the last word.

choices.text: Salute

effects.log: {npc} returns the salute, steppe fashion, a fist to the chest. Then the horse is gone into the grass.

events.text: The campaign against {ct_foe} halts for winter in a valley of reeds. {ct_unit} digs in. Within a month the rice is mouldy, the tents leak, and three men have frostbitten toes. The enemy, presumably, is just as miserable.
events.arc: Winter in the Camp of Reeds

choices.text: Have the men weave reed mats for the tents

effects.log: Reed mats go down on every floor and up every wall. The tents are warm, and smell of a riverbank.

choices.text: Trade with a local village for dry rice (60 taels)

effects.log: The village has rice, and sells it gladly. The men eat well, and the village eats better.

choices.text: Set the men to building a bathhouse

effects.log: A steaming bathhouse rises in the snow, the pride of the army. Other companies visit it like a temple.

events.text: Midwinter. Boredom is now the enemy. Two companies have started a feud over a stolen goose, the officers are gambling away their pay, and a soldier who was once an opera singer offers to stage a play.
events.arc: Winter in the Camp of Reeds

choices.text: Let the opera singer stage the play

effects.log: The singer stages Lady Meng Weeps at the Wall with soldiers in borrowed robes. Hardened veterans weep.

choices.text: Settle the goose feud with a tug of war

effects.log: The two companies pull until the rope breaks. The goose, which was never stolen, watches from a roof.

choices.text: Hold the play in the bathhouse

effects.log: The play runs nine nights in the steam. It is talked of in the army for twenty years.

events.text: Spring comes to the camp of reeds. The ice cracks on the river, the geese come back, and the drums call the army to march. Your men break camp, and a few of them look back at the valley, oddly sorry to leave.
events.arc: Winter in the Camp of Reeds

choices.text: Leave the bathhouse for the village

effects.log: The village takes over the bathhouse and runs it for a century. They call it the Soldiers' Bath.

choices.text: Burn the camp so the enemy cannot use it

effects.log: The camp burns behind you, reeds and all. It is correct, and sad.

choices.text: March out singing

effects.log: The army marches out singing the opera's last song. The geese do not appreciate it.

events.text: Three hundred martial artists from the sects of the southern mountains arrive to join the campaign against {ct_foe}. They are magnificent, proud, and entirely unwilling to march to drums. Their spokesman, Elder Sima, asks where the enemy is, and why everyone is standing in rows.
events.arc: Martial Artists Do Not March in Step

choices.text: Explain the drums to Elder Sima, patiently

effects.log: Sima listens politely, then asks why anyone would wait for a drum to tell them to fight. It is a long afternoon.

choices.text: Order the sect fighters to drill with the ranks

effects.log: The sects drill for one morning. By noon three duels have broken out over who stands at the front.

choices.text: Give the sects their own role: scouts and raiders

effects.log: Sima's eyes light up. Raiders they can be. Within a week, the enemy's supply wagons start vanishing.

events.text: The trouble comes from the other side: your regular soldiers resent the sect fighters, who eat better, fight when they please, and laugh at the drums. One night a brawl breaks out by the cooking fires between a sergeant and a sword disciple.
events.arc: Martial Artists Do Not March in Step

choices.text: Punish both equally

effects.log: Both go without rations for two days. Both sides call it unfair, which means it was fair.

choices.text: Have the sergeant and the disciple spar, properly, in front of everyone

effects.log: They spar for an hour. The disciple wins; the sergeant asks to learn the move. The camp calms.

choices.text: Show the soldiers what the raiders have captured

effects.log: The wagons of enemy grain roll into camp, full. The soldiers eat it, and stop complaining.

events.text: Battle. The enemy breaks through your left line, and the drums call for a reserve that is not there. Across the field, Elder Sima and the sect fighters are watching, unbound by any drum. Dust hides half the field, and the drums sound frantic.
events.arc: Martial Artists Do Not March in Step

choices.text: Signal Sima with a raised banner, the way you talked of

effects.log: Sima sees the banner and leads the sects into the gap like a wave. The line closes.

choices.text: Signal the drill drums and hope

effects.log: The sects stumble into the gap in something like a formation. It is clumsy and it works.

choices.text: Ride to the gap yourself and rally whoever follows

ok.log: Soldiers and sect fighters follow you together. The gap is closed, by both kinds of courage at once.

fail.log: You reach the gap with too few. The line holds only when the sects arrive late.

events.text: When the campaign ends, Elder Sima's sect fighters gather to go home to their mountains, fewer than came. Sima bows to you, as one bows to an equal. "Your drums," Sima says, "are still ridiculous." Then Sima almost smiles.
events.arc: Martial Artists Do Not March in Step

choices.text: Give Sima a drum to take home

effects.log: Sima takes the drum with great seriousness. Years later you hear the sect beats it on festival days.

choices.text: Write the sects' deeds into the official report

effects.log: For once, the sects are named in an imperial report. The mountains do not forget it.

choices.text: Bow back, as to an equal

effects.log: You bow. The soldiers watching see it, and something between the army and the sects shifts a little.

events.text: The demonic sect's stronghold lies at the end of a valley full of green fog. The first patrol into it came back coughing and could not remember their own names for a day. {ct_unit} is ordered to clear a path through.

choices.text: Have every soldier tie a wet cloth over the face

effects.log: The wet cloths help, a little. The men go in coughing and come out coughing, but with their names.

choices.text: Ask a local herbalist what the fog is

effects.log: The herbalist, a stooped woman named Pei, sniffs a jar of it. "Burning ghost-reed," Pei says. "They feed it from the cliffs."

choices.text: Wait for a wind

effects.log: You wait four days for a wind. It comes from the wrong direction, and blows the fog onto your camp.

events.text: Somewhere above the valley, the cult keeps braziers of ghost-reed burning. The fog will not lift while they burn. A narrow goat path climbs the cliff, watched by cult sentries with long hooked spears.

choices.text: Climb the goat path at night with a few volunteers

ok.log: You reach the braziers before dawn and overturn them into a stream. By noon the fog is lifting.

fail.log: A sentry spots you and the volunteers fall back down the path, bruised and coughing.
fail.deathCause: a fall from a cliff, fighting a demonic sect

choices.text: Burn green wormwood upwind, as Pei says, to sweeten the fog

effects.log: Pei's wormwood smoke rolls into the valley and the green turns grey and harmless. The way is open.

choices.text: Push the whole unit through the fog at speed

effects.log: The unit runs through the fog with cloths on their faces. Most come out the other side, dizzy.

events.text: Beyond the fog, at the cult's outer gate, you find a cage of village children, kept as servants by the sect. Their guards have fled. The children stare at the soldiers as if they are another kind of demon.

choices.text: Take the children back through the valley to their villages

effects.log: You march them out yourself. A few cry; most hold soldiers' hands the whole way.

choices.text: Leave them with Pei and press on

effects.log: Pei takes them in with a pot of soup and a stern face. You press on to the inner gate.

choices.text: Ask the children what they know of the stronghold

effects.log: The children know every door and every guard. One draws a map in the ash with a stick.

events.text: The cult stronghold falls, its masters fled into the deeper mountains. The army burns the ghost-reed fields and pulls down the braziers. A last breeze clears the valley, and for the first time in years there is sunlight on the stream.

choices.text: Plant a peach tree by the stream

effects.log: The tree takes root. The villagers come back to the valley within five years and name the stream after it.

choices.text: Record every name of the fallen in the report

effects.log: The report is long. The general signs it without reading, and you read it aloud to {ct_unit} instead.

choices.text: Pay Pei for the wormwood (50 taels)

effects.log: Pei takes the silver and grumbles that it was never about silver. Pei keeps it anyway.

events.text: A figure in the red-black robes of the demonic sect walks into your camp at dawn, hands raised and empty, and sits down by the well. The name given is {npc}, an outer disciple, and the offer is simple: the sect's secret entrance, in exchange for a life.

choices.text: Accept, and keep {npc} under guard

effects.log: {npc} is given a blanket, a bowl and two guards. {npc} eats like someone who has not eaten in days.

choices.text: Ask what made {npc} leave

effects.log: {npc} looks at the well a long time. "They made us drink from a well like this," {npc} says, "after poisoning a village."

choices.text: Send {npc} away: the cult lies

effects.log: {npc} walks out of the camp without a word. Two days later, someone finds a map on your bedroll.

events.text: {npc}'s directions lead to a narrow cleft behind a waterfall. It is exactly as described, and unguarded. The officers are uneasy: an unguarded secret entrance is either a gift from heaven or a trap. The water roars.

choices.text: Send {npc} in first, with your best squad behind

effects.log: {npc} goes in first, walking steadily. The squad follows. There is no trap, only a long dark stair.

choices.text: Scout the cleft yourself before trusting it

ok.log: The cleft is clear. A cult lookout post above it is empty, abandoned in a hurry.

fail.log: You find a tripwire, and spring it. The alarm sounds inside the mountain.

choices.text: Ignore the cleft and assault the main gate

effects.log: The assault is long and costly. {npc} watches from the guard tent and says nothing.

events.text: The stronghold falls. The tribunal of the campaign must decide what to do with {npc}, who wore the robes of a sect that poisoned wells. Your word will weigh more than any other. {npc} sits outside the tribunal tent with folded hands, waiting without complaint.

choices.text: Speak for {npc}'s pardon

effects.log: {npc} is pardoned and given a soldier's papers. Years later you hear of a village healer who will not drink from strange wells.

choices.text: Let the tribunal decide by the law

effects.log: The tribunal sentences {npc} to exile on the frontier. {npc} accepts it with a bow, almost relieved.

choices.text: Take {npc} into {ct_unit}

effects.log: {npc} becomes your quietest soldier. Nobody in the unit ever asks about the robes.

events.text: The village of Black Mulberry, in the shadow of the demonic sect's mountain, will not sell you rice. Its people have red threads on their wrists and a shrine to the sect's founder by the well. They look at the army with cold, frightened eyes.
events.arc: The Village That Prayed to the Sect

choices.text: Pay double for the rice

effects.log: The headman takes your silver without looking at you. The rice is good. The silence is worse.

choices.text: Tear down the shrine

effects.log: The shrine comes down. The villagers watch without a sound, and that night a granary burns.

choices.text: Ask the headman what the sect gives them

effects.log: "Protection," the headman says. "From bandits, from tax men, from you."

events.text: A village girl comes to your tent at night, shaking. The sect takes one child each spring for its inner hall. This spring it is her brother, and the sect's collectors are due in three days. She holds out a red thread, broken.
events.arc: The Village That Prayed to the Sect

choices.text: Set an ambush for the collectors

effects.log: The collectors walk into a ring of spears and surrender at once. The brother goes home.

choices.text: Hide the boy with the army's camp followers

effects.log: The boy wears a cook's apron for a month. The collectors search the village and find no one.

choices.text: Tell the headman you know, and offer the army's protection instead

effects.log: The headman weeps, in front of everyone, for the first time in years. The red threads start to come off.

events.text: When the army marches on, Black Mulberry stands at the roadside to watch. Some still wear red threads. Some do not. The headman walks beside your horse for a li, without speaking. At the edge of the fields an old woman ties a red thread to a fence post, then unties it.
events.arc: The Village That Prayed to the Sect

choices.text: Leave a squad to guard the village until the sect is gone

effects.log: A squad stays behind. In a year, two of the soldiers have married into the village.

choices.text: Rebuild the shrine as a shrine to the earth god

effects.log: The new shrine is plainer, and nobody is taken from it. The villagers come to it slowly.

choices.text: Ride on

effects.log: You ride on. Behind you, the headman stops at the edge of the village and watches until you are gone.

events.text: The drill sergeant of {ct_unit} is {npc}, called Sergeant Gravel by everyone, for the voice. {npc} has picked you out on the first morning, for reasons unknown, and makes you hold a spear at arm's length until the sun moves.

choices.text: Hold the spear without a word

effects.log: You hold it until your arm forgets it is an arm. {npc} walks past twice and grunts, which may be praise.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why you

effects.log: "Because you will be leading these idiots one day," {npc} says. "Hold it higher."

choices.text: Drop it and take the extra drill

effects.log: {npc} gives you the extra drill with real pleasure, and you learn every gate of the camp at a run.

events.text: At the night march, {npc} falls behind the column, limping, an old wound that no one knew about. {npc} orders you on. The column is not allowed to stop for anyone. Rain is coming down sideways, and the column marches with heads low and lanterns hooded.

choices.text: Carry {npc}'s pack and stay alongside

effects.log: You march with two packs to dawn. {npc} says nothing all night, and at dawn says only: "Fool."

choices.text: Obey the order and march on

effects.log: You march on. {npc} catches up at noon, grey-faced, and nods at you for obeying.

choices.text: Report the wound to the captain

effects.log: The captain puts {npc} on a cart. {npc} glares at you from the cart for twenty li.

events.text: {npc} retires that winter, with a pension and a bad leg. On the last day, in front of {ct_unit}, {npc} holds out the old drill spear, the one with the notches, to you. The recruits, who have hated {npc} for years, are suddenly and suspiciously quiet.

choices.text: Take the spear and hold it at arm's length

effects.log: You hold it out, without being told. The whole unit laughs, and {npc} laughs loudest.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay on as an instructor

effects.log: {npc} pretends to think about it for a full breath, then stays. The new recruits will learn to hate both of you.

choices.text: Say what the recruits will never say

effects.log: You thank {npc} in front of everyone. {npc} looks away and says the wind is bad today.

events.text: The rations of {ct_unit} have got worse every month. This week the rice crunches, the pickled radish has a smell of its own, and the cook swears by the stove god that it is the same as last year. It is not.

choices.text: Complain to the squad leader

effects.log: The squad leader complains to the captain, who complains to the quartermaster, who eats very well.

choices.text: Look at the sacks yourself

effects.log: The sacks say First Grade on the outside. Inside is gravel and old rice from the bottom of a barge.

choices.text: Catch fish in the river to add to the pot

effects.log: The squad eats fish for a week. The cook pretends not to notice.

events.text: The trail of the bad rice leads to the quartermaster, Officer Lou, who buys First Grade on paper and Fourth Grade on the barge, and keeps the difference. Lou is the captain's cousin. Lou's own tent smells of roast duck.

choices.text: Take the evidence to the commander directly

effects.log: The commander listens, takes a sack, and tastes it. The commander's face changes.

choices.text: Have the whole squad eat in front of the quartermaster's tent

effects.log: Thirty soldiers eat crunching rice loudly outside Lou's tent. It is very effective theatre.

choices.text: Let it go: Lou is the captain's cousin

effects.log: You eat the gravel. Over time, the gravel eats your teeth.

events.text: Whatever happened, the next delivery of rice comes in clean. The cook tastes it, weeps theatrically, and makes the best congee the camp has seen in a year. The squad looks at you. Even the pickled radish has stopped smelling.

choices.text: Accept the cook's first bowl

effects.log: The congee is excellent. The cook adds a pickled egg to yours for a month.

choices.text: Toast the commander with the congee

effects.log: The commander hears of it and laughs. Lou is moved to a post in a distant salt marsh.

choices.text: Keep a sack of the old gravel as a reminder

effects.log: You keep the sack under your bed. When anyone complains about the food, you show them.

events.text: The soldier on the next sleeping mat is {npc}, from a fishing village, who snores like a gong and shares every parcel from home. In the first month, {npc} teaches you to mend sandals and how to sleep while marching.

choices.text: Share your own pay with {npc}'s family

effects.log: {npc}'s family gets an extra string of coins, and a letter dictated in terrible handwriting.

choices.text: Teach {npc} to read

effects.log: Every night by the fire, you teach {npc} characters. {npc} learns fast and writes home the first letter of a lifetime.

choices.text: Keep a little distance: friends in the ranks die

effects.log: You keep it polite. {npc} notices, and keeps sharing the parcels anyway.

events.text: {npc} has been passed over for promotion three times, and finally loses temper at a squad leader, in front of everyone. The squad leader reaches for a cane. The rules say you should stand still. The whole squad goes silent.

choices.text: Step in front of {npc}

effects.log: The cane lands on you instead. The squad leader stares, then lowers it. {npc} will not look at you for a day.

choices.text: Make a joke loud enough to break the moment

effects.log: The whole squad laughs, the squad leader included. The cane goes back on the hook.

choices.text: Stand still, as ordered

effects.log: {npc} takes ten strokes and walks away stiffly. That night the snoring is quieter.

events.text: Years pass. You and {npc} have marched across half the empire. Then a letter comes: {npc}'s father is dying in the fishing village, and leave is denied. {npc} sits on the mat holding the letter, not crying, not moving.

choices.text: Go to the captain and argue for {npc}'s leave

ok.log: The captain gives {npc} ten days. {npc} arrives in time, and comes back with a basket of dried fish for the whole squad.

fail.log: The captain refuses. {npc} sends a long letter instead, written in the hand you taught.

choices.text: Write the letter home with {npc}, all night

effects.log: You write it together, every word {npc} would have said. The father dies holding it.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} in silence

effects.log: You sit until dawn. Sometimes that is all there is.

events.text: You draw the night watch on the camp palisade of {ct_unit}, the worst post, facing the marsh. At the third hour, something moves in the reeds. It might be an enemy scout. It might be a pig. It might be the owl that has watched you all night.

choices.text: Sound the gong

effects.log: The whole camp turns out in its underclothes. It was a pig. The pig is eaten for breakfast, which helps.

choices.text: Go down to look

effects.log: You go down into the reeds alone with a spear. It is a deserter from the next camp, hungry and shaking.

choices.text: Watch and wait

effects.log: You watch until dawn. Whatever it was goes away. The owl is still there, judging you.

events.text: Your watch partner from the next post, Soldier Bao, has fallen asleep on the palisade three nights running. The punishment for sleeping on watch is the cane, or worse on campaign. Bao has a new baby at home and has not slept in weeks.

choices.text: Cover for Bao and take both posts

effects.log: You walk both posts until dawn, three nights. Bao finds out and cries into a bowl of congee.

choices.text: Wake Bao with a kick and say nothing more

effects.log: Bao stays awake after that, mostly out of fear of you. It works.

choices.text: Report it

effects.log: Bao gets ten strokes and is moved to the kitchens. It is fair, and it is very cold.

events.text: At the last watch of the season, it is not a pig in the reeds. Enemy raiders with torches are coming through the marsh for the horse lines, and you are the only one awake. The owl, for once, has flown.

choices.text: Sound the gong and hold the gap

effects.log: The gong brings the camp at a run. You hold the gap for the time it takes, and the horses are saved.

choices.text: Fight them off alone until help comes

ok.log: You hold three raiders at the gap until the camp arrives. The captain asks your name.

fail.log: The raiders knock you into the mud and run for the horses. The camp catches them at the lines.

choices.text: Bring the deserter you found to guide the camp through the reeds

effects.log: The deserter knows the marsh. Your men go round and catch the raiders from behind.

events.text: Taking over {ct_unit}, you read the payroll. It lists three hundred men. You count them on parade: two hundred and forty. Sixty soldiers exist only on paper, and their pay goes somewhere, every month, very regularly.
events.arc: The Ghost Soldiers of the Payroll

choices.text: Count again, carefully

effects.log: You count three times. Two hundred and forty. The sixty are ghosts, and somebody is feeding them.

choices.text: Ask the paymaster, an old clerk named Ren

effects.log: Ren goes very pale and says the sixty are "on detached duty". All of them, for six years.

choices.text: Keep the sixty on the books and the silver too

effects.log: The silver comes to you now. Ghosts, you discover, are very loyal.

events.text: The ghost pay goes up the chain to the commander's own household. It is how the army has always worked here, Ren whispers. Every officer above you takes a slice, and the ones who refused were posted to the salt marshes.
events.arc: The Ghost Soldiers of the Payroll

choices.text: Report it to the Censorate

effects.log: Your letter goes to the capital with a fast rider. You wait for a salt marsh posting.

choices.text: Use the ghost pay to recruit sixty real soldiers

effects.log: Sixty farm boys join up, and the payroll is true at last. The commander does not notice yet.

choices.text: Take your slice, quietly

effects.log: Your slice is generous. You feel heavier, in more than one way.

events.text: An inspector from the Ministry of War arrives without warning, counts every company of the army, and finds the ghosts everywhere but in {ct_unit}. The commander is arrested. The inspector asks to see you.
events.arc: The Ghost Soldiers of the Payroll

choices.text: Show the inspector your true roll of three hundred

effects.log: The inspector counts three hundred real soldiers. "The only honest roll in the province," the inspector says, and writes it down.

choices.text: Tell the inspector everything

effects.log: The inspector listens to everything, and writes it all. Your name goes to the Ministry as a witness.

choices.text: Say your letter to the Censorate started this

effects.log: The inspector smiles: the letter is in the inspector's sleeve. "It did," the inspector says.

events.text: Old Ren the paymaster retires the year after the ghosts are laid to rest, with a small pension and a large box of ledgers. Before leaving, Ren asks whether you would like to know which officers in the army still keep ghosts of their own.
events.arc: The Ghost Soldiers of the Payroll

choices.text: Take the list

effects.log: Ren's list is short and very precise. You keep it locked away, and somehow every name on it behaves for years.

choices.text: Refuse: you are not the Censorate

effects.log: Ren smiles and burns the list in the brazier. "Wise," the old clerk says. "Lists are heavy."

choices.text: Ask Ren to stay and train an honest paymaster

effects.log: Ren stays two more years and trains a sharp young clerk. The payroll of {ct_unit} stays true long after.

events.text: The remounts for {ct_unit} arrive from the imperial stud: forty horses, of which one is good, ten are old, and the rest look like they were bought from a farmer's cart at night. The horse dealer is already gone.

choices.text: Take the forty and make the best of them

effects.log: You sort them by hand: some will carry, some will pull, and one will charge. It is the army.

choices.text: Send them back with a complaint

effects.log: Your complaint goes to the stud master. Forty worse horses arrive in the spring.

choices.text: Buy better horses at the border market (150 taels)

effects.log: The steppe horses are small, shaggy and tireless. {ct_unit} is the best mounted in the army.

events.text: The one good horse of the forty, a grey mare, will not let anyone ride her but the stable groom, a quiet boy named Duo. The mare bites captains. The mare bit the commander. The commander wants the mare sold.

choices.text: Make Duo a rider

effects.log: Duo rides the mare in the next patrol, bareback, and outruns everything in the army.

choices.text: Try to ride the mare yourself

effects.log: The mare throws you into a water trough. The whole camp has seen it by noon.

choices.text: Sell the mare, the way the commander wants

effects.log: The mare goes to a farmer. Duo cries in the stable. You do not go into the stable for a week.

events.text: Battle. A messenger must cross the field to the other wing with an order, under the enemy's arrows. Your fastest rider will reach it, if any rider can. The order is a single line on a strip of silk, and without it the right wing will be cut off by noon.

choices.text: Send Duo on the grey mare

effects.log: The mare crosses the field like smoke. The order arrives, the wing turns, and Duo comes back grinning.

choices.text: Send a rider on one of the steppe horses

effects.log: The shaggy little horse reaches the other wing without a scratch, unhurried.

choices.text: Ride it yourself

ok.log: You cross the field with arrows in your saddle and none in you. The order arrives.

fail.log: Your horse falls halfway. You run the rest, and arrive late, and out of breath.

events.text: Two of your officers, Liang and Wu, have hated each other since a game of chess in the spring. Now their squads will not share a cooking fire, a well, or a road. In battle, they will not share a flank either, and that will be fatal.
events.arc: The Feud Between Liang and Wu

choices.text: Put their squads side by side on every duty

effects.log: Liang and Wu dig latrines together for a month, in silence. It does not help, but they dig very well.

choices.text: Find out what happened in the chess game

effects.log: Liang says Wu moved a piece while Liang was at the latrine. Wu says the piece moved itself.

choices.text: Transfer one of them to another company

effects.log: Wu goes to another company. The feud follows, by letter.

events.text: The feud reaches the drill ground: Liang's squad deliberately turns left when Wu's turns right, and the whole company ends in a heap. The commander watches from horseback, very quiet. A recruit is still sitting on top of the pile, confused.
events.arc: The Feud Between Liang and Wu

choices.text: Order the whole company to drill until they get it right
