effects.log: The company drills until midnight. By midnight, everyone hates Liang and Wu equally, which unites them.

choices.text: Order a rematch of the chess game, in front of everyone

effects.log: The whole company watches Liang and Wu play for four hours. Nobody blinks; nobody moves a piece wrongly.

choices.text: Demote both to soldier for a month

effects.log: Liang and Wu march in the ranks, side by side, glaring. Their squads learn to work without them.

events.text: In the next battle, Liang's squad is cut off in a ravine. The only squad near enough to reach them is Wu's. You watch Wu look at the ravine, then at you. Arrows are falling into the ravine like rain, and Liang's banner is dipping lower.
events.arc: The Feud Between Liang and Wu

choices.text: Order Wu in

effects.log: Wu goes in without a word, and brings Liang's squad out, Liang on Wu's back with a twisted ankle.

choices.text: Remind Wu the chess game ended in a draw

effects.log: Wu laughs, a short bark, and goes in. "A draw," Wu says to Liang, carrying Liang out.

choices.text: Go in yourself

effects.log: You lead Wu's squad in, and Liang's out. Nobody will ever know if Wu would have gone.

events.text: The throne sends an Army Overseer to your camp: Eunuch Cao, in silk the colour of plums, holding a golden tablet that lets him overrule any general's order. Cao has never seen a battle. Cao would like the tent nearest the river.
events.arc: The Eunuch With the Golden Tablet

choices.text: Give Cao the best tent and every courtesy

effects.log: Cao is charmed and spends a month writing poems about the river. The army is left alone.

choices.text: Give Cao a tent near the latrines, with apologies

effects.log: Cao is not charmed. Letters begin to flow from Cao's tent to the capital, daily.

choices.text: Invite Cao to every council of war

effects.log: Cao attends every council, understands nothing, and agrees with whoever speaks last. You make sure to speak last.

events.text: Cao, tablet raised, orders the army to attack at once, because the court astrologer has declared tomorrow auspicious. The ground is mud; the enemy is fresh; the scouts say wait. The officers in the tent look at their boots.
events.arc: The Eunuch With the Golden Tablet

choices.text: Obey the tablet

effects.log: The army attacks in the mud and is thrown back with heavy losses. Cao writes that the general lacked spirit.

choices.text: Persuade Cao that the stars meant the day after

ok.log: Cao consults a second astrologer, who agrees with you for a modest fee. The army attacks on dry ground and wins.

fail.log: Cao insists. You attack half-heartedly and withdraw without losses or glory.

choices.text: Read Cao one of Cao's own river poems, praising patience

effects.log: Cao is so moved by the reminder of a poem about patience that the attack is postponed. You win in three days.

events.text: The campaign ends. Cao's final report to the throne will decide whether you are a hero or a fool. Cao sits in your tent with brush and ink, and asks, very sweetly, what you think the report should say.
events.arc: The Eunuch With the Golden Tablet

choices.text: Ask Cao to write the truth

effects.log: Cao looks at you for a long time, then writes the truth, mostly. The throne praises you both.

choices.text: Offer Cao a gift for a kind report (150 taels)

effects.log: The report is glowing. Your name is famous at court; so is the size of your gift.

choices.text: Tell Cao the latrine tent was a mistake, and apologise

effects.log: Cao, surprised, accepts the apology. The report is cold, but fair.

events.text: After the victory at Stone Gate, you must write the merit report that decides every promotion in {ct_unit}. Your deputy, General Hua, wants the cavalry named first. The infantry captains want the infantry. The truth is the archers on the hill.

choices.text: Name the archers first

effects.log: The archers on the hill are named first. Hua's cavalry sulk, and the archers are drunk for three days.

choices.text: Name Hua's cavalry first

effects.log: Hua is delighted and loyal. The archers hear of it, and say nothing, very loudly.

choices.text: Name yourself first: it was your plan

effects.log: The report reads like your biography. The capital is impressed. The army is not.

events.text: A minister at court has read the report and writes a private letter: the throne likes a single hero, not a crowd. If the report named only you, the minister hints, a higher seal might follow. The letter is perfumed.

choices.text: Rewrite the report with yourself alone

effects.log: The new report names only you. The seal might follow. The archers, the cavalry and the infantry all read it.

choices.text: Keep the report as it is

effects.log: The minister's letter goes unanswered. Your army notices the report did not change.

choices.text: Reply that every soldier at Stone Gate is the hero

effects.log: The minister reads it to the court as a joke. A few of the court do not laugh.

events.text: At the victory banquet, the captain of the archers, a lean old soldier named Shi, stands up uninvited with a cup. The hall goes silent. Generals do not hear speeches from captains. Shi's cup does not shake.

choices.text: Let Shi speak

effects.log: Shi thanks you for naming the archers, in front of everyone. It is a short speech, and the army remembers it.

choices.text: Raise your own cup to Shi first

effects.log: You toast Shi before Shi can speak. The archers cheer until the lanterns shake.

choices.text: Have Shi sit down

effects.log: Shi sits, without the speech. The hall resumes, a little colder.

events.text: In a skirmish, an arrow comes at the face of the soldier beside you, and your hand moves on its own, as your cultivation taught it to, and catches the arrow in the air. Three soldiers saw. They are staring at your hand, and the arrow in it.

choices.text: Drop the arrow and say it bounced off your helmet

effects.log: "It bounced," you say, and rub your helmet. Two of the three believe you. One does not.

choices.text: Say nothing at all

effects.log: You say nothing. The story goes around the camp anyway, growing every time: a dozen arrows, then a hundred.

choices.text: Laugh and say you were a juggler before the army

effects.log: The soldiers laugh with you. That night they ask you to juggle. You juggle badly, on purpose.

events.text: The soldier who did not believe you, a sharp-eyed archer named Ning, has started watching you: how you breathe on the march, how you never seem tired, how your bowl of congee steams a little more than others.

choices.text: Befriend Ning and tell part of the truth

effects.log: You tell Ning you trained in a temple as a child. It is true, and not all of it. Ning nods, satisfied, for now.

choices.text: Breathe heavily on the march, on purpose

effects.log: You pant and stumble for a month. Ning watches, and frowns: you are a terrible actor.

choices.text: Have Ning moved to another squad

effects.log: Ning is moved. Ning's last look at you is not friendly.

events.text: At the end of the campaign, Ning finds you alone by the river. "I owe you a life," Ning says. "The arrow was for me. Whatever you are, I will not tell anyone." The words hang in the cold air. Ning's breath steams.

choices.text: Thank Ning, and trust the promise

effects.log: Ning keeps it for life. Years later, a retired archer laughs at a story about a juggler, and says nothing.

choices.text: Tell Ning everything

effects.log: You tell it all by the river. Ning listens and is quiet a long time, then asks if you can teach the arrow trick.

choices.text: Deny it to the end

effects.log: "It bounced," you say again. Ning laughs, and walks away still laughing.

events.text: The baggage wagon of {ct_unit} is in the ditch, axle-deep, and six soldiers cannot move it. You could lift it alone, with a breath of qi, and everyone would see. The captain is shouting. It is getting dark.

choices.text: Put your shoulder in with the six and push only as hard as one soldier

effects.log: Seven soldiers push for an hour. The wagon moves, at last, and you are the only one not tired.

choices.text: Wait until the others go for ropes, then lift it alone

effects.log: When they come back with ropes, the wagon is on the road. Nobody can explain it. You shrug a lot.

choices.text: Suggest unloading it first

effects.log: Unloaded, it comes out easily. The captain takes the credit for the idea, loudly.

events.text: The story of the wagon that climbed out of the ditch by itself has reached the camp. The soldiers say a fox spirit lives in the baggage train. They leave little offerings of rice on the wagon at night.

choices.text: Encourage the fox spirit story

effects.log: You add details: the fox has nine tails and hates the captain. The camp adores the fox.

choices.text: Eat the rice offerings

effects.log: The fox spirit, it seems, is hungry. The offerings get bigger.

choices.text: Say nothing and wait for it to pass

effects.log: The story passes, mostly. A few soldiers still bow to the wagon.

events.text: A camp priest arrives to drive out the fox spirit, with bells, smoke and a very loud drum. The whole unit gathers to watch. The priest walks straight up to you and sniffs, thoughtfully. Bells jingle at the priest's belt.

choices.text: Look as foxlike as you can

effects.log: The priest looks at you, laughs, and declares the fox driven out. Then the priest winks.

choices.text: Hold your qi perfectly still

ok.log: The priest sniffs, frowns, and moves on to the cook. The cook is exorcised, protesting.

fail.log: The priest's bell rings by itself as it passes you. The soldiers look at you very strangely for a month.

choices.text: Offer the priest a cup of tea, far from the crowd

effects.log: Over tea the priest says: "Hide it better, friend." And leaves, and that is all.

events.text: The camp wrestling contest of {ct_unit} pits you against Bear Zhang, the biggest soldier in the army. With your cultivation you could throw Zhang over the camp wall. With your cultivation hidden, you need to lose, believably, to a man who smells of onions.

choices.text: Lose slowly and gracefully

effects.log: You lose after a long, convincing struggle. The camp cheers Zhang. Zhang is suspicious about how gentle you were.

choices.text: Win, but only barely

effects.log: You win by a hair, as if by luck. The camp roars. Zhang demands a rematch next year.

choices.text: Pull out with a pretend injury

effects.log: You limp off with a pretend twisted knee. Zhang wins by default, and is disappointed.

events.text: Bear Zhang seeks you out after the contest, onions and all, and says quietly: "You held back. I felt it." Zhang is not clever, but Zhang knows wrestling. Zhang's huge hands are folded like a schoolboy's, waiting for an honest answer.

choices.text: Tell Zhang you held back to spare a friend

effects.log: Zhang thinks about it for a while, then decides it is the nicest thing anyone has ever done.

choices.text: Offer to train with Zhang in secret, at night

effects.log: Zhang agrees at once. Within a year Zhang is the best wrestler in three armies, and owes you everything.

choices.text: Deny it

effects.log: Zhang shrugs. "Fine. Next year, then." You dread next year.

events.text: The next year's contest. Zhang has trained hard. The officers have bets on it. You still cannot show what you are, and Zhang knows it, and is looking at you across the ring with an odd smile. The ring is ringed with soldiers three deep.

choices.text: Lose to Zhang, fairly this time

effects.log: Zhang wins, and lifts you up on one shoulder in front of the whole camp. Nobody suspects anything after that.

choices.text: Fight Zhang to a draw, as trained

effects.log: You and Zhang wrestle to a standstill for an hour. The officers' bets are all lost. Both of you laugh.

choices.text: Win again, by a hair, as last year

effects.log: You win by a hair again. Zhang laughs and says: "Luck, again?" The camp believes it, mostly.

events.text: The deep well of your fortress has always sung, a low echo when the bucket drops. This spring it is quiet. The water is lower each week, and the garrison's old cook says the fortress last went dry the year it fell.

choices.text: Send a soldier down on a rope to look

effects.log: A thin soldier goes down with a lamp and comes up white: a rock fall has blocked the old spring.

choices.text: Ration the water at once

effects.log: One bucket per squad, per day. The garrison grumbles and stays clean only in theory.

choices.text: Have a new well dug inside the walls (100 taels)

effects.log: Diggers come from the town. They dig for a month and find mud, then rock, then nothing.

events.text: The garrison is on half water now. A shepherd from the valley says there was once a second spring under the north tower, sealed by a general a hundred years ago, for reasons the shepherd has forgotten.

choices.text: Clear the rock fall in the old well

effects.log: Soldiers take turns in the dark for a week. On the eighth day, the well sings again.

choices.text: Open the sealed spring under the north tower

effects.log: Under the tower is a stone cistern, full of clear water, and a stone tablet: "For the siege."

choices.text: Haul water up from the valley stream every day

effects.log: A line of mules carries water up the hill all summer. The garrison is tired and alive.

events.text: The fortress has water again, one way or another. The old cook asks, on behalf of the garrison, whether the fortress might hold a small festival for the well, as the old garrisons once did. The garrison has been whispering about it all week.

choices.text: Hold the festival

effects.log: The garrison sings to the well and drops in a coin each. It is silly, and the garrison is happier than in years.

choices.text: Keep the cistern secret: only for a siege

effects.log: Only you and the cook know the tablet's words. The cistern waits under the tower.

choices.text: Have the well cleaned and covered properly

effects.log: The well gets a new stone lid and a bronze bucket. It sings deeper than ever.

events.text: The beacon at Wolf Rock, three li from your fortress, is the first of a chain that carries warning to the capital in a single night. Its two old keepers have just lit it by mistake, for a forest fire. Six beacons down the line have answered.

choices.text: Ride to the next beacon to stop the chain

effects.log: You ride through the night and reach the third beacon too late. The capital wakes up for an invasion that is not coming.

choices.text: Send a fast rider with a correction to the capital

effects.log: The correction arrives a day behind the alarm. The capital is embarrassed, then angry.

choices.text: Light a second fire beside the first, the old signal for 'false alarm'

effects.log: The keepers remember the old signal. Down the line the beacons dim, one by one. Only one keeper had forgotten.

events.text: The Ministry of War sends an inspector to find out who lit the beacon. The two old keepers, Grandfather Ou and Grandfather Lü, have kept it for forty years. They sit in your hall and shake with fear. Lü keeps apologising to the tower.

choices.text: Take the blame yourself

effects.log: You tell the inspector the error was yours. The inspector writes it down. The keepers will not stop bowing.

choices.text: Tell the truth: a forest fire, an honest mistake

effects.log: The inspector accepts it, grudgingly, and orders new keepers. Ou and Lü are retired.

choices.text: Argue that an early warning is better than a late one

effects.log: The inspector, unexpectedly, agrees, and writes a memorial praising the speed of the chain.

events.text: Next autumn, real riders come over the mountains, thousands of them, on a moonless night. The new keepers of Wolf Rock are young and asleep. Your watch sees the riders' torches before anyone. The chain must be lit now, or never.

choices.text: Ride to Wolf Rock yourself and light the beacon

effects.log: You light it with your own hands. Down the chain the fires leap, and by dawn the capital knows.

choices.text: Send for Grandfather Ou and Grandfather Lü

effects.log: The two old keepers climb the tower in the dark faster than the young ones and have it lit in moments.

choices.text: Light a beacon on the fortress wall instead

ok.log: The next beacon sees your fire and answers. The chain runs, a little late, but it runs.

fail.log: The next beacon thinks it is another false alarm, until the riders reach it.

events.text: The enemy comes down the valley at dawn, more of them than the fortress has arrows. By noon they have ringed the walls and begun building siege ladders from the orchard below. The relief army is twenty days away, if it comes at all.

choices.text: Count the arrows, the rice and the water

effects.log: Rice for thirty days, arrows for ten, water if the well holds. You write it all on the wall in chalk.

choices.text: Burn the orchard before they finish the ladders

effects.log: Fire arrows set the orchard alight. The ladders burn with it, and the enemy must go to the far woods for timber.

choices.text: Send a rider through the lines to hurry the relief

effects.log: Your best rider goes out at dusk, low over the horse's neck. Nobody knows whether the rider got through.

events.text: Day twenty. The ladders come at night, three times, and three times the garrison throws them back. The arrows are gone; the soldiers are throwing roof tiles. The well is low, and the men are drinking half a bowl a day.

choices.text: Tear down the empty barracks for stones and tiles

effects.log: The barracks come down tile by tile. Nobody sleeps under a roof, and the walls hold.

choices.text: Open the old cistern under the north tower

effects.log: The cistern under the tower is full. The garrison drinks, and cheers, and fights on.

choices.text: Lead a night sortie to burn their camp

ok.log: You burn their food stores and come back with half your men. The enemy is hungry now, too.

fail.log: The sortie is caught in the open. You make it back over the wall, wounded and alone.
fail.deathCause: a night sortie from a besieged fortress

events.text: Day forty. On the far hills, banners. The relief army is here. The enemy breaks camp in a hurry and is gone by evening, leaving the burned orchard and their dead. The garrison stands on the wall, too tired to cheer.

choices.text: Open the gates and greet the relief army

effects.log: The relief general rides through your gate and stops, looking at the stripped barracks and the thin soldiers. The general salutes.

choices.text: Find out what happened to your rider

effects.log: The rider got through, the relief general says, and rode the last ten li on foot after the horse fell. The rider lives.

choices.text: Climb down and plant an orchard sapling

effects.log: You plant the first sapling yourself, in the ash. The garrison plants the rest without being told.

events.text: Every spring, steppe traders bring horses, felt and cheese to the foot of your fortress wall, to trade for tea, silk and iron pots. This spring they have brought a great deal of horses, and a complaint: your gate guards take a tax of their own.

choices.text: Investigate the gate guards

effects.log: The gate guards have been taking one cheese in ten for years. Your cellar, it turns out, is full of cheese.

choices.text: Lower the market tax to keep the traders happy

effects.log: The traders cheer and bring twice as many horses. The treasury grumbles.

choices.text: Tell the traders the tax is the tax

effects.log: The traders shrug and trade anyway, but the price of horses goes up.

events.text: At the market, a steppe trader and a tea merchant from the south are about to come to blows over a horse that the tea merchant says is lame and the trader says is merely thoughtful. The horse itself gazes into the distance.

choices.text: Ride the horse yourself and judge

ok.log: The horse is not lame. It is merely very thoughtful. The sale goes through, at a thoughtful price.

fail.log: The horse is lame, and also throws you into a felt stall. The market laughs for a week.

choices.text: Make them split the difference

effects.log: Both men are equally unhappy, which is the market's definition of fairness.

choices.text: Pay the cheese back to the traders first, then judge

effects.log: The cheese goes back to its owners, cartload by cartload. The traders accept any judgment of yours after that.

events.text: At the end of the market, the steppe chief who leads the traders invites you to a feast in their felt tents below the wall, an honour never offered to the commander before you. The traders watch to see whether you will come down from the wall.

choices.text: Accept, and go without guards

effects.log: You eat roasted mutton and drink fermented mare's milk, and learn more about the steppe in a night than in a year of reports.

choices.text: Accept, and bring a gift of tea (40 taels)

effects.log: The tea is the best of the south. The chief keeps it under the tent pole like a treasure.

choices.text: Decline politely: a commander should not leave the wall

effects.log: The chief understands, and sends a whole roasted sheep up to the gate instead.

events.text: The next spring the steppe chief does not come to the market. A young rider comes instead, the chief's grandson, with the chief's horsehair banner and a message: the old chief has died over the winter, and asked that you be told before anyone else.

choices.text: Ride down and pour tea on the grass for the old chief

effects.log: You pour the best southern tea on the grass, steppe fashion. The traders watch in silence, then bow.

choices.text: Open the market tax-free this year, in mourning

effects.log: The market is the biggest in memory. The grandson trades shrewdly and thanks you gravely.

choices.text: Ask the grandson to keep the old peace

effects.log: "The peace was his," the grandson says. "Now it is mine." The grandson holds out a hand, and you take it.

events.text: Winter at the fortress. The snow comes over the walls in drifts, the wind cuts through armour, and the coal ships from the river are frozen in two days away. The garrison is burning the last of the firewood, and furniture is next.
events.arc: The Coldest Winter on the Wall

choices.text: Send soldiers to the frozen ships to haul the coal on sledges

effects.log: Twenty soldiers haul coal on sledges for a week. They come back blue and heroic.

choices.text: Have the whole garrison sleep together in the great hall

effects.log: Three hundred soldiers sleep in one hall, snoring in harmony. Nobody freezes; nobody sleeps.

choices.text: Burn the old wooden gate tower

effects.log: The gate tower burns through the worst week. You will need a new gate tower in spring.

events.text: Midwinter. The garrison is bored and cold. A soldier proposes a snow-sculpture contest between the towers. Another proposes an ice-fishing contest on the moat. A third proposes a tug of war with the cooks.
events.arc: The Coldest Winter on the Wall

choices.text: The snow sculptures

effects.log: The north tower builds a snow dragon; the south tower builds a snow version of you. The south tower wins.

choices.text: Ice-fishing on the moat

effects.log: The moat yields three carp and a very old helmet. The carp are eaten; the helmet is hung in the hall.

choices.text: The tug of war with the cooks

effects.log: The cooks win. Nobody is surprised. Everyone eats less that week.

events.text: At last the thaw. The ships come in with coal, the walls drip, and the garrison looks thin but whole. At the spring parade, the old cook asks to say a word on behalf of the garrison. The cook's apron is very clean for the occasion.
events.arc: The Coldest Winter on the Wall

choices.text: Let the cook speak

effects.log: The cook says: "Nobody froze." Then sits down. It is the best speech you have ever heard.

choices.text: Give the coal haulers a medal each

effects.log: Twenty wooden medals, carved by the cook. The coal haulers wear them for the rest of their lives.

choices.text: Order a new stock of firewood stored for next year

effects.log: By autumn a mountain of firewood stands in the courtyard. The garrison sleeps easier just looking at it.

events.text: After the spring rains, a crack opens in the east wall of your fortress, wide enough for a soldier's fist. The master mason, an old woman named Dou, puts her ear to it and says the wall is old and tired, and needs a season and three hundred taels.
events.arc: The Crack in the East Wall

choices.text: Pay Dou to rebuild it properly (300 taels)

effects.log: Dou's crew takes down the old stones one by one and builds them back with lime and rice paste. It will stand a century.

choices.text: Patch it with mud and timber for now

effects.log: The patch looks solid from the outside. Dou sniffs at it and says nothing.

choices.text: Ask the capital for funds

effects.log: Your request joins a pile in the Ministry of War. The crack, unimpressed, widens.

events.text: A steppe rider is seen in the hills, looking at your walls through a long tube. You know exactly which wall the rider is looking at. The rider stays on the ridge all afternoon, unhurried, and leaves at dusk. The next day the rider is back, at the same rock.
events.arc: The Crack in the East Wall

choices.text: Hang a great banner over the east wall

effects.log: A huge banner hides the crack from the hills. The rider looks at the banner for a long time.

choices.text: Station your best soldiers on the east wall

effects.log: The east wall bristles with spears. If the rider wanted to know where your strength is, the rider knows now.

choices.text: Let the rider look: the wall is new

effects.log: The rider sees fresh stones and lime, and rides away disappointed.

events.text: The raid comes in autumn, a sharp hard rush at the east wall, as you expected. The steppe riders throw grapnels and ropes at the spot where the crack was. Their war cries carry across the valley long before they reach the ditch.
events.arc: The Crack in the East Wall

choices.text: Hold the east wall with everything

effects.log: The riders throw themselves at the wall for an hour and fall back. The wall holds, and Dou watches from the gatehouse, satisfied.

choices.text: Lead a sally out of the north gate to take them in the flank

ok.log: You hit the riders in the flank and they scatter. The east wall did not even need to hold.

fail.log: The sally is spotted and driven back. The east wall holds anyway, barely.

choices.text: Bring Dou to the wall to see her work hold

effects.log: Dou stands on the wall she built while the ropes slide off it. "Rice paste," Dou says, and goes back to bed.

events.text: The only road from {ct_fief} to the county town is a cart track that turns into a river every spring. Merchants will not come; farmers lose a day carrying beans to market. Road Master Tian from the county says forty li of stone road would change everything, and cost almost everything.

choices.text: Commission the road (200 taels)

effects.log: Tian unrolls the plans across your hall floor. Stone, gravel, ditches, and twelve small bridges.

choices.text: Ask every village to give ten days of labour instead

effects.log: The villages grumble, then turn out with shovels. The road will be slower, and theirs.

choices.text: Leave the track as it is

effects.log: Every spring the track becomes a river again, and every spring someone loses a cart in it.

events.text: Eleven li along, the line of the new road runs straight through the old graveyard of Plum Hollow, where the families of three villages have buried their dead for two hundred years. The diggers have stopped and are standing with their caps off.

choices.text: Bend the road around the graveyard

effects.log: The road bends in a long, graceful curve. It costs a month and a bridge, and the three villages bow to you at the curve.

choices.text: Move the graves with full rites, at your expense (60 taels)

effects.log: Monks chant for nine days as the families move their dead to a hill with a better view. Nobody is happy; nobody is angry.

choices.text: Run the road straight through

effects.log: The road runs straight. The villages never walk that stretch at night, and an old woman curses it daily.

events.text: The road is finished: forty li of grey stone, twelve bridges, and a stone post every li with the distance carved on it. Road Master Tian suggests a toll gate at the county end, to pay the road back. The merchants suggest otherwise.

choices.text: Set a modest toll

effects.log: The toll is small and the carts are many. In five years the road has paid for itself, and the toll keeper is very fat.

choices.text: Keep the road free

effects.log: Merchants come from three counties to use the free road. The markets of {ct_fief} fill, and so, slowly, does the treasury.

choices.text: Free for those who built it, a toll for everyone else

effects.log: Every villager who dug gets a wooden token. They show it at the gate with enormous pride.

events.text: Along the new road comes something nobody expected: a retired scholar from the capital, Master Ouyang, who finds the road so pleasant that the old scholar stops at its end and asks to open a school in {ct_fief}. Ouyang has no money, only books.

choices.text: Give Ouyang an empty granary for the school

effects.log: The granary fills with children and the smell of ink. Ouyang teaches poetry to farmers' children, and they are good at it.

choices.text: Pay Ouyang a teacher's salary (40 taels)

effects.log: Ouyang accepts with dignity and buys more books with all of it.

choices.text: Send Ouyang on to the county town

effects.log: Ouyang walks on, cheerful, with the books. The county town gets a very good school.

events.text: Ten years after the first stone. The road is worn smooth in the middle by cart wheels, the li-posts are mossy, and the children of {ct_fief} walk it every autumn to sit the county exam, and some of them pass.

choices.text: Walk the road yourself, all forty li

effects.log: You walk it in a day, alone, touching each li-post. At the end, a carter offers you a lift home, not knowing who you are.

choices.text: Celebrate the first scholar from Ouyang's school

effects.log: A farmer's girl from the bean fields passes the county exam. The whole fief walks her to the road's end and back.

choices.text: Repair the bridges before they need it (50 taels)

effects.log: Masons go over every bridge, stone by stone. The road will outlast everyone who walks it.
